## Natural history notes

A small to medium-sized owlet moth characterized by mottled brown to grayish-brown wings, fine wavy crosslines, and a somewhat angular resting posture that gives the wings a bent or folded appearance. In Florida, it is found in wooded and shrubby habitats, especially humid forest edges, hammocks, wetlands, parks, and other areas with leaf litter and understory vegetation. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on dead leaves and some living plant material, helping move decomposing vegetation into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
